deed: דונה גרציה נשיא מבריחה מאות אנוסים מהאינקוויזיציה בספינות התבלינים שלה
title: Doña Gracia Nasi smuggled conversos away from the Inquisition among the spices on her merchant ships

trailer.text: According to the encyclopedia Women in World History, Doña Gracia Nasi was the leading businesswoman of her day, and according to the National Library of Israel she was considered the richest woman in the world in the 16th century.
According to Aish, she was born in 1510 in Portugal, into a secret Jewish family, and her legal name was Beatrice de Luna.
According to My Jewish Learning, she created a secret network that enabled conversos to leave Portugal and to transfer their money through bills of exchange.
According to Aish, her agents smuggled secret Jews across borders along with the spices and gems, and according to Hidabroot, Jews were hidden as stowaways on her merchant ships.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, she later settled with her daughter Reyna in Constantinople and there openly confessed her Judaism.

paragraphs.text: According to the Jewish Encyclopedia (1906), Gracia was a member of the Spanish family of Benveniste and was born about 1510, probably in Portugal.
According to Aish, she was born into a secret Jewish family, and her legal name was Beatrice de Luna.
According to My Jewish Learning, Beatrice married another converso, Francisco Mendes, a wealthy trader in gems and spices.
According to Women in World History, in 1536 an office of the Inquisition was established in Lisbon.
According to Halakha of the Day, that year the papal pressure grew, and the court of the Inquisition was established in Lisbon.
According to Halakha of the Day, Francisco Mendes died and left his position and his fortune to his wife.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, in 1536 Gracia fled with her only daughter Reyna and several relatives to Antwerp, where many conversos were then staying.

stations.title: The network: people among the goods

paragraphs.text: According to Women in World History, Gracia and her brother-in-law organized a Jewish underground in Antwerp using their business connections.
According to My Jewish Learning, the secret network enabled conversos to leave Portugal and to transfer their money through bills of exchange.
According to Aish, her agents smuggled secret Jews across borders along with the spices and gems.
According to Hidabroot, Jews were hidden as stowaways on her merchant ships.
According to the author Michal Aharoni-Regev, as quoted by Ynet, Gracia smuggled Jews using bribes to innkeepers, monasteries, port personnel and ship captains.
According to Hidabroot, a separate network moved the Jews' property out of Spain and Portugal by sophisticated means.

According to Halakha of the Day, Gracia's company bought and sold the properties of conversos in Portugal before the Inquisition confiscated them, and the money reached its owners through the Mendes bank.
According to Aharoni-Regev in Ynet, Gracia sent agents with promissory notes to the value of the fugitives' property.
According to Aish, the historian Cecil Roth wrote in 1946 that Gracia was the "brains" behind the elaborate organization.

stations.title: From Antwerp to prison in Venice

paragraphs.text: According to the National Library of Israel, Emperor Charles V proposed marrying off Reyna, then 15, to Duke Fernando de Aragón.
According to the National Library of Israel, Gracia declared that her daughter had been kidnapped by her cousin, who loved her, and this was part of an escape plan.
According to the National Library of Israel, the legal struggle with Charles V ended when Gracia agreed to give him an interest-free loan for two years.
According to both encyclopedias, the death of her brother-in-law Diogo delayed her departure from Antwerp.
According to the National Library of Israel, she traveled overland from Antwerp to Venice at the head of a large convoy, with official permission from Queen Mary.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, her younger sister denounced her to the Venetian authorities as a secret Jewess who intended to flee to Turkey with her wealth.
According to Women in World History, Brianda Mendes publicly denounced her as a Jew.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, the King of France and the Senate of Venice confiscated the property of the Mendes family and imprisoned Gracia in Venice to prevent her flight.
According to both encyclopedias, the sultan's physician, of the Hamon family, came to her aid.
According to Women in World History, Ottoman protests and numerous bribes secured her release.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, after her release she immediately went to Ferrara, and there she acknowledged that she was a Jewess.

stations.title: In Constantinople: openly and with an open hand

paragraphs.text: According to Women in World History, in Ferrara Gracia shed her Christian guise and proclaimed her faith in Judaism.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia, she settled with Reyna in Constantinople and there openly confessed her Judaism.
According to Women in World History, she was acknowledged there as the leader of the Jewish community and settled in the district of Galata.
According to Women in World History, she organized a consortium of Muslims and Jews in Istanbul to trade in spices, wheat and wool.
According to the same encyclopedia, she funded Jewish hospitals and schools, supported Jewish students, and funded the translation and printing of Jewish books.
According to Aish, each day 80 poor people entered her palace to receive free meals.
According to Hidabroot, in the harsh winter of 1567 Gracia bought clothing and firewood for the poor.
According to Aish, in 1559 she established a synagogue in Salonika, a city in which many conversos from Spain found refuge.
According to My Jewish Learning, in 1553 the Hebrew Bible was translated into Spanish and published in two editions, and it was called the Ferrara Bible.
According to the National Library of Israel, Gracia donated a significant sum to fund the printing of the converso Bible by Abraham Usque and Yom Tob Atias.

stations.title: The boycott of the port of Ancona

paragraphs.text: According to the Women's Encyclopedia, in 1555, at the instigation of the Inquisition, 24 Jews were burned in Ancona, and 100 more were imprisoned.
According to Women in World History, Gracia organized an international boycott of the port of Ancona.
According to the same encyclopedia, she recruited Sultan Suleiman, and even dictated the stern letter he sent to the pope.
According to Women in World History, the boycott was at first strongly felt in Ancona: many Christian merchants went bankrupt, and there was a severe shortage of Turkish goods.
According to the same encyclopedia, the boycott collapsed, but no cargo of the Mendes family passed through the port of Ancona again.
According to Hidabroot, Gracia received permission from Sultan Suleiman to rebuild Tiberias, in return for a thousand ducats a year.
According to My Jewish Learning, she leased the land in Tiberias for a high rent that she paid herself, and briefly turned the city into a thriving Jewish city.
According to Ynet, she and her son-in-law sent money to the region, built homes, inaugurated a synagogue and began building a wall around the city.
According to Ynet, she fulfilled her husband's will and moved his remains from Lisbon.
The sources disagree on where he was reburied.

stations.title: The end of the road, and the memory

paragraphs.text: According to Hidabroot, Doña Gracia died not far from Constantinople, before fulfilling her dream of going to the Land of Israel.
According to Ynet, Irit Ahdoot speculates that Gracia may have been poisoned.
According to the Jewish Encyclopedia (1906), she made great sacrifices to prevent the introduction of the Inquisition into Portugal, and was the "guardian angel" of the conversos.
According to Arutz 7, President Shimon Peres marked 500 years since her birth at the President's Residence.
According to Arutz 7, Peres said that when Gracia decided to return to the ancient homeland, she became the first Zionist.
In 2010, issue 213 of "Et-Mol" published an article marking 500 years since her birth.
According to Jewish Currents, New York declared a Dona Gracia Day in June 2010, and Philadelphia followed suit a year later.
According to Ynet, Gracia did not enter the Israeli collective memory.
According to Women in World History, many Jews wondered whether the boycott of Ancona was not in fact hurting the city's Jews, whom they sought to protect.
According to Ynet, many rabbis supported the step, but many Jews in Ancona opposed it, fearing for their livelihoods.
According to My Jewish Learning, Gracia's appointment to manage Diogo's share caused a bitter fight between her and Brianda that had effects for years.
According to Ynet, the Jews did not respond enthusiastically to her calls to settle in the Land.

versions.says: Ynet: her father, Álvaro de Luna, was a doctor, and her mother, Felipa, was from the wealthy Benveniste family
Women in World History: her parents are unknown

disagreements.question: In what year did Francisco Mendes die?

versions.says: Women in World History: in 1536, suddenly
Halakha of the Day: in 1538

disagreements.question: How many people did Gracia save?

versions.says: Jewish Currents: hundreds of conversos who fled Spain and Portugal to Antwerp
Aish: thousands of Jews
Halakha of the Day: tens of thousands of conversos, from death, misery and slavery
According to Ynet's subheadline, she helped hundreds of thousands of Jews, but the body of the same article says that she saved thousands of Jews.
Women in World History: in 1543
Jewish Encyclopedia: about 1545

disagreements.question: When did Gracia arrive in Venice and get imprisoned there?

versions.says: Women in World History: in 1545 she was imprisoned in Venice, and the Mendes family assets were frozen
Jewish Encyclopedia: only in 1549 was she able to travel to Venice with her daughter and her widowed sister

disagreements.question: When was Gracia released from prison in Venice?

versions.says: Jewish Encyclopedia: about 1550
Women in World History: in 1549

disagreements.question: In what year did Gracia settle in Constantinople?

versions.says: Jewish Encyclopedia: in 1552
Women in World History: in 1553

disagreements.question: How many Jews were burned in Ancona, and in what year?

versions.says: Women in World History: 24 Jews in 1555, and 100 more were imprisoned
Jewish Currents: 25 conversos in 1556

disagreements.question: In what year did Gracia receive permission for Tiberias?

versions.says: Hidabroot: in 1561, to rebuild the city
According to the Women's Encyclopedia, in its account of her life, in 1565 Gracia received special permission from Suleiman to establish a new Jewish settlement in Tiberias.
Aish: in Tiberias
Ynet: on the Mount of Olives in Jerusalem
Women in World History: in the Jehoshaphat Valley outside Jerusalem

disagreements.question: In what year did Gracia die?

versions.says: Hidabroot and the Jewish Encyclopedia: in 1569
According to Halakha of the Day, the body of the article gives her years as 1510–1568.
Women in World History: at her request, she was buried beside her husband in the Jehoshaphat Valley
Ynet: her burial site is unknown to this day
Irit Ahdoot, as quoted by Ynet: her burial place was deliberately concealed

disagreements.question: What was the name of the nobleman who sought to marry Reyna?

versions.says: National Library of Israel: Duke Fernando de Aragón, and Reyna was then 15
My Jewish Learning: the Catholic nobleman Don Francisco d’Aragon, in 1536

unknowns.text: It is not known exactly how many people passed through the escape network; the sources give numbers very far apart from one another
It is not known where Gracia was buried
It is not known how long the Jewish city in Tiberias lasted; it is said only that it was briefly

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, גרציה נשיא הייתה אשת העסקים המובילה בדורה.
claims.quote: Gracia Nasi was the preeminent business-woman of her day.

claims.text: לפי הספרייה הלאומית, היא נחשבה לאישה העשירה בעולם במאה ה-16.
claims.quote: was considered the richest woman in the world in the 16th century.

claims.quote: She was born into a secret Jewish family in Portugal in 1510 and given the royal-sounding name of Beatrice de Luna as her legal name

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, ביאטריס יצרה רשת סודית שאפשרה לאנוסים לעזוב את פורטוגל ולהעביר את כספם בשטרות חליפין.
claims.quote: Beatrice created a secret network, enabling Jewish conversosto leave Portugal, transferring their money through bills of exchange

claims.text: לפי Aish, בזמן שסחרה בתבלינים ובאבני חן, סוכניה הבריחו יהודים סודיים מעבר לגבולות יחד עם הסחורה.
claims.quote: While she traded spices and gems, her business agents also ferried secret Jews across borders along with this merchandise.

claims.text: לפי הידברות, יהודים הוחבאו כנוסעים סמויים על ספינות הסוחר שלה.
claims.quote: על ספינות הסוחר שלה הוחבאו יהודים כנוסעים סמויים, כאשר עובדיה

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית (1906), ב-1552 התיישבה גרציה עם בתה ריינה בקושטא והודתה שם בגלוי ביהדותה.
claims.quote: In 1552 she settled with her daughter Reyna at Constantinople and there also openly confessed Judaism.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית (1906), גרציה, פילנתרופית ממשפחת בנבנישתי הספרדית, נולדה בסביבות 1510, כנראה בפורטוגל, ומתה בקושטא ב-1569.
claims.quote: Philanthropist; born about 1510, probably in Portugal; died at Constantinople 1569; member of the Spanish family of Benveniste.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, ב-1536 הוקם משרד אינקוויזיציה בליסבון ובאותה שנה מת פרנסיסקו מנדס בפתאומיות והותיר אותה אלמנה.
claims.quote: On May 23, an office of the Holy Inquisition was established in Lisbon. As well, Francisco Mendes died suddenly, leaving her a widow.

claims.text: לפי Halakha of the Day, ב-1536 גברה הלחץ האפיפיורי ובית הדין של האינקוויזיציה הוקם בליסבון.
claims.quote: finally, in 1536 the papal pressure prevailed and the dreaded court was installed in Lisboa.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית (1906), היא ברחה ב-1536 עם בתה היחידה ריינה וכמה קרובים לאנטוורפן, שבה שהו אז אנוסים רבים.
claims.quote: together with her only daughter Reyna and several relatives, she fled in 1536 to Antwerp, where many Maranos were then sojourning

claims.quote: Thus was Dona Gracia able to travel overland from Antwerp to Venice at the head of a large convoy, with official permission granted by Queen Mary herself.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית (1906), גרציה שוחררה בסביבות 1550 ויצאה מיד לפרארה, שם הודתה שהיא יהודייה.
claims.quote: Meanwhile Gracia was liberated (c. 1550) and immediately went to Ferrara, where she acknowledged herself to be a Jewess.

claims.quote: New York City designated a Dona Gracia Day in June 2010, and Philadelphia followed suit a year later.

claims.quote: Beatrice married another converso, Francisco Mendes, a wealthy trader in gems and spices.

claims.quote: In 1538 Francisco Mendes passed away, and he left his position and his fortune to his wife Beatriz.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, גרציה וגיסה ארגנו באמצעות קשריהם העסקיים מחתרת יהודית באנטוורפן.
claims.quote: Using their extensive business connections, Gracia and her brother-in-law organized a Jewish underground.

claims.quote: רשת נפרדת עסקה בהוצאת רכושם של היהודים אל מחוץ לספרד ולפורטוגל, באמצעים מתוחכמים של הלבנת הון

claims.quote: In 1559, Gracia established a synagogue in Salonika, in Greece, a city in which many secret Jews from Spain were finding refuge.

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, ב-1553 תורגם התנ"ך לספרדית ופורסם בשתי מהדורות, ונקרא תנ"ך פרארה.
claims.quote: In 1553 the Hebrew Bible was translated into Spanish and published in two editions, one for Christians and one for Jews.

claims.text: לפי הספרייה הלאומית, גרציה תרמה סכום משמעותי למימון הדפסת תנ"ך האנוסים בידי אברהם אושקי ויום טוב אטיאס.
claims.quote: Dona Gracia donated a significant sum of money to fund the efforts of Abraham Usque and Yom Tob Atias, who sought to print a converso bible.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, ב-1555 נשרפו באנקונה 24 יהודים בהמלצת האינקוויזיציה ו-100 נוספים נאסרו.
claims.quote: At the instigation of the Inquisition, 24 Jews were burned to death in Ancona, while 100 more were imprisoned.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, גרציה ארגנה חרם בינלאומי על נמל אנקונה.
claims.quote: Nasi undertook the organization of an international boycott against Ancona

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, גרציה גייסה את סולימאן ואף הכתיבה את המכתב החריף ששלח לאפיפיור.
claims.quote: She recruited Suleiman to assist her, and even dictated the stern letter which he dispatched to the pope.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, בתחילה הורגש החרם בעוצמה באנקונה: סוחרים נוצרים רבים פשטו רגל והייתה מחסור חמור בסחורות טורקיות.
claims.quote: Initially, the boycott was strongly felt in Ancona. Many bankruptcies occurred among Christian merchants, and there was a severe shortage of Turkish goods.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, החרם על אנקונה קרס, אך סחורה של משפחת מנדס לא עברה עוד בנמל אנקונה.
claims.quote: The measure proved ineffective, and at length the boycott collapsed. No cargo owned by the Mendes family, however, ever passed through the port of Ancona again.

claims.text: לפי הידברות, ב-1561 קיבלה גרציה אישור מהסולטן סולימאן לבנות מחדש את טבריה תמורת אלף דוקטים לשנה.
claims.quote: בשנת 1561 היא קיבלה אישור מהסולטן סולימן לבנות מחדש את העיר טבריה, תמורת אלף דוקטי זהב לשנה.

claims.text: לפי Ynet, גרציה וחתנה שלחו כסף לאזור, בנו בתים, חנכו בית כנסת והחלו לבנות חומה סביב העיר.
claims.quote: Doña Gracia and her son-in-law sent money to the region, built homes, inaugurated a synagogue, and start building a wall around the developing city.

claims.text: לפי Ynet, היא מילאה את צוואת בעלה והעבירה את שרידיו מליסבון להר הזיתים בירושלים.
claims.quote: reinterring his remains, from a church cemetery in Lisbon, to Jerusalem’s Mount of Olives

claims.text: לפי Aish, גרציה הוציאה את גופת בעלה מבית קברות בליסבון והביאה אותו לקבורה מחדש בטבריה.
claims.quote: Now, with great difficulty, she had his body removed from the church graveyard in Lisbon where it was interred and brought to Israel, where he was reburied in Tiberias.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, גופת בעלה הועלתה מליסבון ונקברה בעמק יהושפט מחוץ לירושלים.
claims.quote: his body was exhumed and transported to Palestine, where it was interred in the Jehoshaphat Valley, outside of Jerusalem.

claims.text: לפי הידברות, דונה גרציה נפטרה ב-1569 לא רחוק מקושטא, בטרם הגשימה את חלומה לעלות לארץ ישראל.
claims.quote: אולם ב-1569 נפטרה דונה גרציה לא רחוק מקושטא, בטרם הגשימה את חלומה לעלות לארץ ישראל.

claims.text: לפי Ynet, אחדות משערת שגרציה אולי הורעלה, ומאמינה שהאפיפיור פאולוס הרביעי אחראי למותה.
claims.quote: Although Gracia lived to 59, considered advanced at the time, Ahdoot proposes she may have been poisoned

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית (1906), היא עשתה הקרבות גדולות כדי למנוע הכנסת האינקוויזיציה לפורטוגל והייתה 'המלאך השומר' של האנוסים.
claims.quote: She made great sacrifices to prevent the introduction of the Inquisition into Portugal, and was the guardian angel of the Maranos.

claims.text: לפי ערוץ 7, נשיא המדינה שמעון פרס ציין במשכן הנשיא 500 שנה להולדתה של דונה גרציה.
claims.quote: נשיא המדינה שמעון פרס ציין היום במשכן הנשיא 500 להולדתה של אשת העסקים דונה גרציה

claims.text: לפי ערוץ 7, פרס אמר שכשהחליטה גרציה לשוב למולדת העתיקה היא הייתה לציונית הראשונה.
claims.quote: כשהחליטה לשוב למולדת העתיקה ולחדש המורשת הגדולה, היא הייתה לציונית הראשונה

claims.text: ב-2010 פורסם בגיליון 213 של 'עת-מול' מאמר לציון 500 שנה להולדת דונה גרציה נשיא.
claims.quote: יהודים ואנוסים, בסתר ובגלוי - 500 שנה להולדת דונה גרציה נשיא

claims.text: לפי Ynet, גרציה לא נכנסה לזיכרון הקולקטיבי הישראלי.
claims.quote: Sadly, this formidable woman never made it into the Israeli collective memory.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, יהודים רבים הטילו ספק אם החרם אינו פוגע דווקא ביהודי אנקונה שאותם ביקשו להגן עליהם.
claims.quote: Many Jews, both inside the Ottoman Empire and without, wondered aloud whether they were not merely hurting those they sought to protect

claims.text: לפי Ynet, רבנים רבים תמכו בצעד, אך יהודים רבים באנקונה, מחשש לפרנסתם, התנגדו לו.
claims.quote: Numerous rabbis supported the daring step, but many Jews in Ancona, fearing for their own livelihoods, were against it.

claims.text: לפי My Jewish Learning, מינוי גרציה למנהלת חלקה של דיוגו גרם לריב מר בינה לבין בריאנדה, שהשפעותיו נמשכו שנים.
claims.quote: This assignment caused a bitter fight between Beatrice and Brianda that had ramifications for many years afterward.

claims.text: לפי Ynet, היהודים לא נענו בהתלהבות לקריאותיה להתיישב בארץ.
claims.quote: The Jews did not respond enthusiastically to her calls.

claims.text: לפי Ynet, אביה, אלברו דה לונה, היה רופא ואמה, פליפה, הייתה ממשפחת בנבנישתי העשירה.
claims.quote: Her father, Álvaro de Luna, was a doctor and her mother, Felipa, hailed from the wealthy Benveniste family.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים בהיסטוריה העולמית, הוריה אינם ידועים.
claims.quote: Born Beatrice de Luna in Portugal in 1510; died in 1569 in Istanbul, Turkey; buried in Jehoshaphat Valley, Palestine; though parents unknown

claims.text: לפי Jewish Currents, היא פיתחה רשת בריחה למאות אנוסים שנמלטו מספרד ומפורטוגל לאנטוורפן.
claims.quote: had developed an escape network for hundreds of conversos fleeing Spain and Portugal to Antwerp

claims.text: לפי Aish, גרציה נשיא התריסה נגד האינקוויזיציה הספרדית והעבירה אלפי יהודים למקום מבטחים.
claims.quote: Gracia Nasi defied the Spanish Inquisition to ferry thousands of Jews to safety.

claims.text: לפי Halakha of the Day, גרציה הצילה ממוות, מעוני ומעבדות עשרות אלפי אנוסים.
claims.quote: to rescue and save from death, misery, and slavery tens of thousands of

claims.text: לפי Ynet, היא הייתה האישה העשירה בעולם וסייעה למאות אלפי יהודים.
claims.quote: was the richest woman in the world who helped hundreds of thousands of Jews against the leader of the Christian world

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, ב-1545 נאסרה גרציה בידי השלטונות בוונציה ונכסי משפחת מנדס הוקפאו.
claims.quote: In 1545, Nasi was imprisoned by Venetian authorities, and all of the Mendes family assets were frozen.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית (1906), רק ב-1549 הצליחה גרציה לנסוע עם בתה ואחותה האלמנה לוונציה.
claims.quote: It was not until 1549 that she was able to go with her daughter, her widowed sister, and the latter

claims.text: לפי Jewish Currents, 25 אנוסים נשרפו על המוקד באנקונה ב-1556.
claims.quote: Twenty-five crypto-Jews were burned at the stake in Ancona, Italy on this date in 1556.

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, ב-1565 קיבלה גרציה אישור מסולימאן להקים יישוב יהודי חדש בטבריה.
claims.quote: In 1565, Nasi obtained special permission from Suleiman to build a new Jewish settlement at Tiberias, in Palestine.

claims.text: לפי Halakha of the Day, שנות חייה היו 1510-1568.
claims.quote: Doña Gracias Mendes (1510-1568), also known as Doña Gracia Nasí, was probably the woman who did the most for the Jewish people

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה לנשים, לבקשתה נקברה גרציה ליד בעלה בעמק יהושפט.
claims.quote: At her request, she was buried beside her husband in the Jehoshaphat Valley of Palestine.

claims.text: לפי Ynet, מקום קבורתה של גרציה אינו ידוע עד היום.
claims.quote: Her own burial site is unknown to this day.

claims.text: לפי אירית אחדות, כפי שצוטטה ב-Ynet, מקום קבורתה הוסתר במכוון.
claims.quote: Her final resting place was deliberately made to disappear.

claims.text: הספרייה הלאומית: הדוכס פרננדו דה ארגון, וריינה הייתה אז בת 15
claims.quote: marry off the 15-year-old Reyna to Duke Fernando de Aragón

claims.quote: a Catholic nobleman, Don Francisco d’Aragon, sought Reyna’s hand in marriage
